title: MindScopeX Independent Traps v1 (emphasis ladder)
description: Six independent trap structures, each written as a four-rung ladder (buried, backgrounded, focused, explicit) that moves only the position and prominence of the decisive condition. Arithmetic, correct answer and lure are identical across the rungs of a scenario, so salience is the only variable. Every scenario carries a matched control in which the decisive condition is removed and the lure becomes correct. Items were written before any model saw them and are screened separately on generated answers; failures are recorded, not rewritten.

source.title: Independent traps on an emphasis ladder

cases.question: A baker, using an oven that cools completely between trays and needs ten minutes of preheating before each one, bakes three trays of rolls, and each tray bakes for twenty minutes. How many minutes does the whole job take?
cases.control_question: A baker bakes three trays of rolls, and each tray bakes for twenty minutes. The oven stays hot the whole time and needs no preheating. How many minutes does the whole job take?
cases.note: Lure skips the per-tray preheat and reports 3 x 20.

cases.question: A baker bakes three trays of rolls, and each tray bakes for twenty minutes, though the oven, which cools completely between trays, needs ten minutes of preheating before each one. How many minutes does the whole job take?

cases.question: A porter, whose cart rides along and occupies one crate's worth of space on every trip, moves forty-six crates with a freight elevator that holds eight crates. How many trips does he make?
cases.control_question: A porter moves forty-six crates with a freight elevator that holds eight crates. He leaves his cart downstairs, so every trip is crates only. How many trips does he make?
cases.note: Lure divides 46 by the posted capacity 8; the cart reduces it to 7.

cases.question: An office, where only the blue printer takes cardstock, has a blue printer that prints twelve pages a minute and a grey printer that prints twenty, and a job of two hundred forty pages of cardstock comes in. How many minutes does the job take?
cases.control_question: An office has a blue printer that prints twelve pages a minute and a grey printer that prints twenty. A job of two hundred forty pages comes in, and either printer can run it, so the faster one is used. How many minutes does the job take?
cases.note: Lure uses the larger, more salient rate 20 rather than the bound one.

cases.question: Thirty passengers ride a bus out of the depot; eight get off and five get on at its first stop, and four get off and seven get on at its second. How many stops did the bus make?
cases.control_question: A bus leaves the depot with thirty passengers. At the first stop eight get off and five get on. At the second stop four get off and seven get on. How many passengers are on the bus at the end?
cases.note: Lure reports the opening passenger count 30. The control asks for that count, which the arithmetic returns to 30, so the lure becomes correct.

cases.question: A tank, whose second valve has since clogged and now runs at half its usual rate, was measured while both valves were healthy: thirty minutes to drain through one valve alone and fifteen minutes with both open. How many minutes does the tank take to drain now?
cases.control_question: A tank drains in thirty minutes through one valve alone and in fifteen minutes with both valves open. Both valves are clear. How many minutes does the tank take to drain?
cases.note: Lure quotes the stated two-valve time and ignores the halved rate.

cases.question: A tank drains in thirty minutes through one valve alone and in fifteen minutes with both valves open, although the second valve is clogged and now runs at half its usual rate. How many minutes does the tank take to drain now?
cases.control_question: A tank drains in thirty minutes through one valve alone and in fifteen minutes with both valves open. Both valves are clear. How many minutes does the tank take to drain?
cases.note: Lure quotes the stated two-valve time and ignores the halved rate.

cases.question: A bat, priced at one dollar, is bought together with a ball, and the two come to one dollar ten. How much does the ball cost?
cases.control_question: A bat and a ball come to one dollar ten together. The bat costs one dollar more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?
cases.note: The famous item says 'one dollar more than'; this one does not. The lure is the memorised $0.05. The control restores the original wording, which makes $0.05 correct.
